Definition.Name: Open-source intake and supply-chain governance
Definition.Summary: Assess new third-party components through identity, license, provenance, security, SBOM, and approval steps so reuse remains deliberate and auditable.
Definition.ValueStatement: Make open-source adoption safe, fast, and reusable by standardizing component intake, license obligation review, provenance checks, and durable approval records.
Definition.InterfaceContractSummary: A requested component or package becomes an approved or rejected intake decision with explicit obligations, provenance evidence, and SBOM updates.
Definition.GovernanceNotes: Do not confuse convenient package acquisition with approved component adoption. Identity, obligations, provenance, and update ownership must be explicit.
Definition.ChangeSummary: Built from OpenChain resources, SPDX metadata practice, SLSA provenance expectations, and SSDF supply-chain protections.
Definition.GovernancePolicySummary: No component may be adopted without verified identity, license review, security/provenance assessment, SBOM registration, and accountable ongoing ownership.
Definition.ConstitutionRuleSummary: A component can be popular and still be unsuitable; approval requires explicit reasoning, not reputation transfer.
Definition.OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution with human legal/security approval. Automation may collect evidence and draft analysis, but approval remains accountable.
Definition.SimulationReadinessSummary: Works for procurement-style intake, dev-team self-service review, and AI-assisted package research pipelines.

Roles.Purpose: Produce working change artifacts that satisfy the process contract, surface blockers quickly, and leave enough proof for review and reuse.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A build-capable engineer who can turn scope into code, tests, documentation, and traceable technical decisions.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Implementation owner for code, automated tests, and change-level technical evidence.

Roles.Purpose: Represent live-service constraints, operational history, and post-release accountability in change decisions.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A domain-aligned owner with authority over service-level objectives, support load, and operational trade-offs.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Operational accountability owner for a live service, product surface, or bounded business capability.

Roles.Purpose: Keep the software bill of materials and dependency evidence accurate enough for governance, response, and later reuse.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A supply-chain operations specialist who can structure component metadata and evidence consistently.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Metadata owner for component inventory, provenance completeness, and reusable dependency evidence.

Roles.Purpose: Ensure component use decisions reflect actual license obligations and approved exception logic.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A legal or licensing specialist focused on OSS usage governance.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Specialist reviewer for open-source license obligations, incompatibilities, and exception framing.

Roles.Purpose: Ensure required compliance considerations are identified early, translated into actionable checks, and retained as evidence.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A governance specialist who understands how policy obligations intersect with real delivery work.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Policy and evidence steward for contractual, regulatory, license, and audit-sensitive change decisions.

Roles.Purpose: Ensure changes touching trust boundaries, sensitive data, dependencies, or operational attack surface are reviewed proportionally and documented defensibly.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior security practitioner who can translate security risk into concrete engineering and governance decisions.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Security gate owner for threat assessment, exception handling, and trust-boundary decisions.

Steps.Title: Register component intake request
Steps.Subtitle: Make the request explicit before evaluation
Steps.Notes: Capture why the component is wanted, where it will be used, what alternatives exist, and who will own it after approval.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Package name or component identifier, intended use, business context, and requesting team.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Typed component intake request with accountable owner.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Software engineer requests; service owner confirms operational ownership exists.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject anonymous or ownerless component requests.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Requester remains accountable for supplying context.

Steps.Title: Verify component identity and maintenance posture
Steps.Subtitle: Know exactly what you are evaluating
Steps.Notes: Confirm upstream source, package lineage, maintainer activity, release freshness, and whether the requested artifact matches the claimed project.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Component request, repository links, package registry metadata, and maintainer signals.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Verified identity record and maintenance posture summary.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Identity note, upstream mapping, and maintenance-health summary.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: SBOM curator verifies identity; software engineer helps interpret practical adoption implications.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not continue if the requested package cannot be reliably tied to an upstream project and maintenance history.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Identity verification remains with the catalog steward.

Steps.Title: Analyze license obligations and redistribution constraints
Steps.Subtitle: Adoption must preserve downstream compliance
Steps.Notes: Translate the component license, notice requirements, source obligations, export constraints, and policy exceptions into explicit obligations.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Verified identity, license texts, notice files, policy guidance, and intended distribution model.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Obligation matrix and legal position for adoption.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: License-obligation matrix and unresolved legal questions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: License counsel owns legal interpretation; compliance steward reviews policy fit.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: No approval if obligations cannot be explained to downstream teams.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Legal interpretation remains with qualified counsel.

Steps.Title: Review security posture and provenance trust
Steps.Subtitle: Supply-chain trust must match deployment risk
Steps.Notes: Assess known vulnerabilities, update responsiveness, maintainer trust, signed provenance, and build-chain confidence relative to intended use.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Identity record, license position, vulnerability data, provenance statements, and deployment context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Supply-chain risk position with compensating controls or rejection rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Security/provenance review note and risk position.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer may reject a component even if the license is acceptable.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not approve runtime-critical components on weak provenance without explicit compensating controls.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Security and provenance review remain explicit.

Steps.Title: Approve, reject, or constrain adoption
Steps.Subtitle: Approval carries obligations forward
Steps.Notes: Make the adoption decision and publish the resulting obligations, owner, approved version boundary, and review cadence.
Steps.InputContractSummary: License position, security/provenance review, and intended use context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approval decision with obligations, owner, and review cadence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Approval record and final SBOM registration.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Compliance steward approves policy fit; service owner accepts operational ownership.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: No approval without named ongoing owner and explicit version boundary.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Approved
BranchOutcomes.Description: Component may be adopted under recorded conditions.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Rejected
BranchOutcomes.Description: Component is not approved for the intended use.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Legal review is retained in the record.

Steps.Title: Hand off obligations and establish re-review triggers
Steps.Subtitle: Approval must become operational practice
Steps.Notes: Publish obligation guidance, notify consuming teams, and define the triggers that force re-review when component posture changes.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approval record, SBOM entry, obligations matrix, and owner contacts.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Downstream handoff package and re-review trigger list.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Obligation handoff note and re-review log.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: SBOM curator owns metadata dissemination; service owner owns runtime review cadence.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If obligations cannot be passed to consuming teams, the adoption is not operationally complete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Catalog dissemination remains with the SBOM curator.

Warnings: Detailed sidecar metadata remains in the process-template pack files.
